Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for 3-day history of severe, persistent headache with photophobia and visual disturbance; clinician impression possible migraine; plan for in-person neurologic and fundoscopic exam, analgesic trial, and safety-netting.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe “blinding” headache for 3 days, continuous, interfering with ability to work/concentrate.
- Onset/timeline: Sudden onset upon waking 3 days ago; persistent daily since.
- Location/character: Global headache, worse over right supraorbital region; described as stabbing at times when standing quickly or moving head.
- Severity: Typically 8/10, reduced to ~5/10 with ibuprofen but not fully resolving.
- Modifying factors:
  - Exacerbating: Bright light (photophobia), rapid standing, head movement.
  - Relieving: Partial relief with ibuprofen.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Visual: “Shooting light”/odd visual sensations; recent optometry check reportedly normal, no change in vision prescription.
  - Nausea: Denied initially but later stated “feeling a bit sick”; no vomiting. (conflict noted)
  - Sleep: Able to fall asleep; not woken by headache; may wake in the morning with headache.
  - No focal neurologic symptoms: No tingling, numbness, or weakness.
  - No URI/sinus symptoms: Denies sore throat, ear pain, sinus pain, cough, phlegm.
  - No epistaxis or hemoptysis.
  - Systemic: No reported fever (temperature not checked). No weight change. Reports low energy likely due to headache.
- Functional impact: Works from home; took 1 full day off; could not complete work this morning due to headache.
- Prior headaches: Intermittent brief headaches previously, typically ≤2 days and responsive to ibuprofen; no prior similar severity; no prior visual symptoms, nausea, or vomiting with past headaches.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- Remote history of unspecified pain in youth; no cause found; resolved.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Medications:
- Oral contraceptive pill (specific name/type not captured); started ~1 year ago; no perceived side effects; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen as needed for headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- New prescription planned: “Stronger” NSAID alternative to ibuprofen; dose/route/frequency not documented. May take acetaminophen concurrently; instructed to take with food.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Occupation: Works from home.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks alcohol; approximately “three … once a week” (exact type/units not clearly stated).
- Recreational drugs: Denies.
- Recent travel: No recent travel abroad.

Family History:
- Mother with migraines (severe, with vomiting).
- No other family history reported.

Physical Examination:

Investigations:
- Recent optometry/eye check: Reported normal; no change in vision prescription (date not specified).
- Blood pressure: Reported normal at pharmacy ~1 year ago when starting oral contraceptive; no recent measurement.
- No labs or imaging performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute severe persistent headache with photophobia and visual disturbance; possible migraine-type headache (first episode of this severity; ongoing for 3 days).
  - Plan:
    - Arrange in-person appointment for full neurological examination and fundoscopic exam (to evaluate for papilledema or other ocular findings).
    - Start prescribed stronger NSAID (name not documented) in place of ibuprofen; may combine with acetaminophen; take with food.
    - If symptoms resolve before appointment, cancel; if headache worsens, becomes unbearable, or changes in character, go to the emergency department (A&E) for urgent assessment; may call clinic for further advice.
- Issue 2: Contraceptive management in context of possible migraine with aura (flashing lights).
  - Plan:
    - Check blood pressure at in-person visit.
    - If migraine with aura is confirmed, current pill may be unsuitable; discuss alternative contraception and make changes as appropriate.
    - Continue current pill for now.
- Issue 3: Work/functional impact due to headache.
  - Plan:
    - Symptomatic management as above; reassess functional status at follow-up after examination and treatment trial.

General plan items:
- Safety-netting: Seek urgent care if red flags develop (worsening/unbearable pain, new neurologic deficits, persistent vomiting, fever, or change in character).
- Follow-up: Book with support team for in-person exam and BP check; contact clinic if questions or deterioration.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals (BP, HR, temp) not obtained.
  - Neurological and fundoscopic exam not performed (planned).
  - Medication details incomplete: oral contraceptive name/type and all dosing details not documented; newly prescribed NSAID name/dose/route/frequency not documented; ibuprofen dosing not documented.
  - Exact alcohol quantity/type unclear.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Nausea: Initially denied, later reported “feeling a bit sick” without vomiting. Conflict noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Some audio gaps/inaudible segments (name of contraceptive pill and exact alcohol details unclear).
